change.title: Durabilize non-one-click destructive mutation receipts
change.summary: Implements the bounded P2-B source slice for mode, settings, applied-profile revoke, Codex authentication, and Codex network mutations. The Desktop now uses one credential-free config-mutation-operation.v1 receipt with a sibling exact Config fence, bounded per-effect checkpoints, terminal clearing tombstone, and fail-closed boot recovery; intent-only profile surfaces return typed outcomes without claiming a receipt. Codex login additionally persists inert sidecar identity and matching start authorization before network work. P2-A, one-click/history journals, credentials, real providers, installed artifacts, signing, and release remain separate evidence boundaries.

basis: exact P2-A source candidate 09cbc686c61228eba592475dec6e9e327658b4a2 is the frozen implementation base
credential-free receipt and Config-fence unit tests cover bounded size, no-clobber CAS, clearing tombstone, mutual exclusion, orphan recovery, receipt-only corruption, and ordinary-writer blocking
auth start tests serialize the bounded start write against supervisor cancel and native exit, then preserve the post-start cancel channel
auth stream tests consume buffered events, reap protocol errors, persist exact in-progress identity for login and logout, and require exact signal identity for every auth sidecar
Codex network UI accepts only receipt-free exact committed intents for non-destructive writes or operation-id-bound exact completed terminal receipts for destructive writes
mode-switch UI accepts only the exact set_mode intent outcome or the exact destructive set_mode_official terminal outcome before publishing the selected mode
settings, clear-key, and delete UI consumers distinguish exact committed/no-change intents from exact completed destructive terminal outcomes before publishing success state
non-destructive set_settings and active-profile selection propagate the actual atomic Config update result into committed versus no_change intent disposition
Codex login success, failure, cancellation, protocol-error, and logout terminal receipts derive stopped versus preserved runtime state from the actual fenced preflight action

auth failure-seam tests cover reservation release, terminal PID clearing, dynamic after-image drift, logout in-progress identity, terminal mutation-ID binding, generation references, and dual-receipt boot conflict
frontend and preview tests parse only safe typed envelopes and reject attention or malformed responses
no artifact, installed App, live provider, live Science, credentials, signing, notarization, or public release evidence is claimed
